utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case next on the list.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Case IT-02-60-A, the Prosecutor versus Blagojevic and Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I have an apology to make to all counsel who are involved in this case. That is, we are a few minutes late, and I beg of you to overlook that circumstance, this being attributable to a deficiency in the arrangements on the part of the secretariat of the Court. I hope this will be conveyed to the Registrar and we will avoid a repetition of that in future. Now, I welcome you all. This is a Status Conference at the appeals stage in the case of the Prosecution against Blagojevic and Jokic. I would like to begin by ensuring that the audio equipment is working properly. So in the usual way, may I ask the appellant, Mr. Jokic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT JOKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can hear you in a language I understand, as well as in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about counsel? The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: We can hear. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Next, I would like to call for appearances. Mr. Murphy, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, yes, Your Honour. Peter Murphy, counsel for Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And with you?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Your Honour. Chrissa Loukas, co-counsel for Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. And for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to my learned colleagues. Norman Farrell, and with me is the case manager Lourdes Galicia, Mr. Milbert Shin, and Mr. Matteo Costi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel, as you are aware, Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires that Status Conferences be held for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody at intervals no greater than 120 days. We held a Status Conference for Mr. Jokic's co-appellant, Mr. Blagojevic, on 13 March this year, but postponed Mr. Jokic's due to his change in counsel. The last Status Conference in Mr. Jokic's case was on 23 September, 2005. Mr. Jokic waived the application of the 120-day Rule so as to accommodate several recent delays in his Status Conference, mostly relating to the recent change in his assigned counsel. We have new counsel with us today. I welcome very especially Mr. Murphy, Mr. Jokic's new lead counsel. I also welcome Ms. Loukas, who is returning as his co-counsel after a hiatus from the case. Let me begin by ask Mr. Jokic if he has any concerns to raise with respect to the conditions of his detention.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT JOKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no complaints. The conditions are good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then that brings me to the principal order of business today, which is to address the next steps to be taken in bringing this appeal toward a hearing in light of the change in counsel. I will first update the parties as to the status of the case and then invite them to raise any concerns they have. Mr. Blagojevic and the Prosecution have both filed appeals in this case, as has the co-appellant Vidoje Blagojevic. Now, I find that the judgement of the Trial Chamber in this case was delivered on 17th of January, 2005, and a written judgement then followed on the 24th of January, 2005. The Prosecution filed its notice of appeal on 23 February, 2005, and its appeal brief on 9th of May, 2005. Both Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Jokic filed their briefs in response to the Prosecution's appeal on 20 June, 2005. Mr. Jokic also filed his notice of appeal on 23 February, 2005. Mr. Blagojevic filed his notice of appeal on 31 May, 2005. As I have said, we are not dealing with Mr. Blagojevic's case now. The briefing on the Prosecution's appeal was thus already complete prior to the last Status Conference, and the briefing on Mr. Blagojevic's appeal was completed on 28 December, 2005. In Mr. Jokic's appeal, the Prosecution filed its consolidated response brief on 16 December, 2005, but Mr. Jokic has not filed a reply as yet. On the 6th of January, 2006, Mr. Jokic's prior counsel filed a notice of her intention not to file a reply and instead to reply to the Prosecution's argument at the oral proceedings. There have been a number of procedural decisions filed since the last Status Conference which need not be exhaustively summarised here. They include decisions relating to Mr. Jokic's provisional release for a memorial service last fall, decisions relating to the motions of the accused in other cases for access to certain confidential materials, and decisions relating to extensions of time and page limits. They also include decisions relating to the pleadings in Mr. Jokic's appeal. In particular, Mr. Jokic was permitted to file various amendments to his notice of appeal and ordered to make certain corresponding changes to his appeal brief. I take it that all of these decisions and the related filings are available to new counsel so that they can familiarise themselves with the procedural history of the case and put themselves in order to answer the case. What I would like to do now is to get an idea from Mr. Murphy as to what further filings he anticipates making in this case and how much time he thinks it will be necessary for him to have. I must caution that this is only a preliminary discussion for informational purposes. As counsel will appreciate, any new submissions or requests for extension of time must be submitted in writing according to the normal procedures. Then the Prosecution and Mr. Blagojevic will have a chance to respond in writing. Mr. Murphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Appeals Chamber will be aware that the pleadings filed so far on behalf of Mr. Jokic by prior counsel were the subject of certain responses from the Prosecution and also comments by the Appeals Chamber. In -- in the light of that, Your Honour, Ms. Loukas and I have made a careful analysis of what seem to us to be the issues, with the advantage of having access to all the previous filings that Your Honour mentioned, and also, in both our cases, with a certain prior familiarity with the case. In Ms. Loukas's case as co-counsel; in my case, Your Honour, some time ago as legal consultant for Mr. Jokic at the pre-trial stage. And based upon that analysis, we have -- we are in a position today to address Your Honour about our proposed conduct of the case from this moment on. Your Honour, I have given Mr. Farrell advance notice of what I'm about to say, and I have also supplied Mr. Roberts with what I will call a very rough draft of a proposed revised notice of appeal. Your Honour, this is not a filing, it's simply a note which I hope will be of assistance to Your Honour in following the matters that I will address. Your Honour, it's our view that it would be in the interests of justice and also greatly simplify the task of the Appeals Chamber and perhaps the Prosecution, as well as the Defence, if we were to file in due course a revised notice of appeal and appellate brief. We will, of course, as Your Honour says, file a motion. At this point I'm only giving the Court an outline of our intentions. Briefly, Your Honour, we -- we believe, as I think the Appeals Chamber did also, that there was a certain lack of clarity in the filings that have been made to this point, and we believe that if allowed to file a revised notice of appeal and appellate brief, we can achieve two major goals. The first would be to -- to simplify and clarify the issues. It seems to us, Your Honour, that there were a number of issues, or at least allegations made in the notice of appeal and the brief that need not be pursued in the sense that they have no -- in our judgement, have no reasonable prospect of success, and we would, therefore, propose to delete those and then that would simplify the task considerably. The second -- well, going along with that, what we would come to, Your Honour, would effectively be five grounds of appeal, two legal -- well, three legal and two factual, which are summarised in the note that I handed up to Your Honour today. And obviously we will work on a little more formal language for some of this, but really it would simplify, I think, and consolidate the issues into those grounds of appeal that have a reasonable prospect of success and would greatly simplify matters. I think I'm right in saying, Your Honour, that with respect to these grounds of appeal, only one would really represent perhaps something of a surprise to the Prosecution in being a new ground of appeal. It is the third legal ground on the second page of the note, and in fact this ground is mentioned in the appellate brief, so it is in fact there but it is not treated as a separate ground and the Prosecution I think could have been forgiven for overlooking its significance the way matters stand now. Ms. Loukas and I believe, however, that this is a substantive ground of appeal in its own right that should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Is it paragraph (b), beginning with the words, "The Trial Chamber erred in law ..."?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. It's under the heading "Third Ground of Appeal."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Oh, third ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: On the second page, Your Honour, yes. And it has to do with the law recording circumstantial evidence in the Tribunal. As Your Honour knows, in the Celebici case, a certain rule was laid down about the handling of entirely circumstantial cases, which we believe this to be. And so with that exception, we believe the other grounds of appeal, although they may be set out in a different order, have already been articulated and briefed. So we recognise that some additional burden will be placed on the Prosecution in responding to this, but on the other hand, we think that that burden will be relatively light and certainly would be offset by the -- by the fact that a great deal of unnecessary material will be deleted. The second advantage, Your Honour, would be this: That in the course of filing, we will, of course, automatically cure the defects which the Appeals Chamber has drawn attention to before in the numbering of the paragraphs, references to pages of the judgement, the correspondence between the notice of appeal and the appellate brief. These are all matters that the Appeals Chamber had occasion to comment on in the procedural rulings. And if I may say it in this way, Your Honour, that is what I would like to call Plan A. Obviously, we will be dependent on the Appeals Chamber's agreement with us that it would be in the interests of justice and of fairness to Mr. Jokic to permit that course of action. Plan B, if I can so describe it, Your Honour, would be to -- as far as possible, to deal with the matters that should have been dealt with already in the existing notice of appeal and appellate brief, and that would include certainly a motion to file a reply out of time. We take the view, Your Honour, that a reply should have been filed in this case. It would be our intention to file a motion for leave to file one. And at the same time, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Is that very usual, Mr. Farrell, for an appellant not to file a reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: You've obviously been on the Bench hearing appeals longer than I've been arguing here, but in, I think, the seven years here I don't think I recall one, quite honestly, where they did not file a reply. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, my experience has been some the same as Mr. Farrell's, and certainly Ms. Loukas and I take the view that a reply should have been filed. Also implicit in Plan B, of course, would be that the formal defects in the notice of appeal and the brief will be corrected as far as that can be done. And however on any view, Your Honour, Plan B will still leave -- leave all of us picking between different documents in order to see what has gone before and to make sense of the issues. So it would be our submission, Your Honour, we will file -- it's our intention very soon to file a motion in which I anticipate we would ask for the following relief: To be allowed within a reasonable time - and I'm very mindful of time here; we would probably ask, I think, for 45 days, not longer - to file --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: 45, did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. From the date when the motion is granted, Your Honour. And we would file at the same time the notice of appeal and the brief. We would not wait, of course, for any additional period of time. We would file both of the documents together. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I'm only asking that because I think you would have gathered from the paperwork that it was the general intention to have the hearing of this appeal during the first six months of this year, if possible. That's not possible any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: But we need not postpone the hour of reckoning too far.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Indeed. We're conscious also of the interests of Mr. Blagojevic in this, Your Honour, that clearly he has an interest also in having the appeal heard as soon as possible. And what we will -- and that's why we're anxious not to delay. Your Honour, our submission, briefly, will be -- will be this, that the paramount interest here will be -- should be the interests of justice and of fairness to Mr. Jokic, and while we obviously recognise that this is a matter within Your Honour's discretion and within the discretion of the Appeals Chamber, it would be our submission that those interests in this case, as well as perhaps the interests of ease in identifying the issues which will assist the Appeals Chamber in due course, Your Honour, we would suggest that the balance of those interests would be in favour of allowing us to do that. But failing that, Your Honour, it would be our intention, within the same time frame, of course, to implement what I've called Plan B, to make sure that all the points that the Appeals Chamber has drawn attention to this in case that need correction will be corrected within -- within a reasonable time. And, Your Honour, that really is our submission as to the way in which we would like to conduct the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you a lot, Mr. Murphy. That's very helpful. I must say to you, Mr. Farrell, that Mr. Murphy has seemed to make out a good case based on the grounds of a simplification and clarification of issues. What do you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In terms of the Plan B, the intention to file a reply and to deal with matters that should have been dealt with before, Mr. Murphy was kind enough to phone me yesterday. We discussed the matters and, as a general matter, I don't think he'll get much opposition from the Prosecution in terms of things that -- well, another counsel may have done if in the shoes of the previous counsel and as these counsel would like to do. So in terms of that matter, I think we'll just wait until we get their filing, and generally I think if they feel it's necessary in the interest of their client, I don't think you'll get much opposition from the Prosecution. In relation to the first issue, I haven't had the chance, of course, to look -- I do appreciate the importance of simplification and deletion of grounds for appeal from any Defence brief, but I haven't had the chance to look at it and of course would appreciate the time, as I'm sure Mr. Murphy understands, to look at the additional ground that they have proposed before responding, but I'll wait for the filing from Mr. Murphy and I'm certainly available, as is the Prosecution team, to meet with both Mr. Murphy and Ms. Loukas at their convenience to try and resolve some of the other matters that may arise as they prepare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, we have every indication of willingness to cooperate. That's very welcome to the Court. You will make your applications in due course to the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: We will, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: It will receive such consideration as on the merits will be due to the applications. Will there be any further motions made this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Not on behalf of the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then we may close the proceedings? Thank you very much.

procedural_notes.text: [The Appellant Blagojevic not present in court]
